tasks.short: Check and label images from the procedure, enter procedure codes, complete the procedure documentation, check the record, and close the exam for billing.

steps.what: Sonographer processes images from procedures and types patient details onto them
Sonographer codes the procedure for billing
Sonographer completes appropriate documentation of the procedure
Sonographer checks the record before closing the exam: procedure code, documentation and images against the exam done
Sonographer closes the checked exam and releases it for billing

tasks.design: The ultrasound machine takes patient and order data from the radiology worklist ({OTHER}), so images carry the right patient and exam without typing. A rule set proposes the procedure code from the order and exam type, and the sonographer confirms it. The sonographer documents the procedure as today in a template per exam type, checks the record and closes the exam once for billing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patient details were typed on the machine and codes looked up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Modality worklists and rule-based code proposals are standard in radiology systems.
tasks.still_hard: Combined or unplanned procedures do not match the rule set.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing an image labelled with the wrong side before it reaches the radiologist.
tasks.altitude: The sonographer confirms data and codes instead of typing them.

evidence.claim: DHD codes day admissions to ICD-10 from clinical text in 32 hospitals.
Modality worklists pass patient and order data to imaging machines; codes can be proposed by fixed rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the procedure done to the exam closed; billing itself is outside.
Input contract: orders in the radiology system; code rules set by the billing team; fallback is typing and look-ups.

The sonographer confirms every code; checking and closing keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because patient data come from the worklist and image processing stays; s2 keeps 30 for confirming the proposed code; s3 keeps 85 because the template gives only the layout and standard fields.
research_questions: Do coding corrections by billing fall?

incremental.description: Sonographer corrects codes for combined procedures.

approvals.approved_version: The exam record with procedure code, documentation and images exactly as checked by the sonographer in s4, closed and released once to billing; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many combined procedures fall outside the code rules (s2 keeps 60) and the template saves little (s3 keeps 95) (22.7); high: standard exams that match the rules (32.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The sonographer keeps checking images and records; typed patient details and code look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A sonographer with more time for patients.
